novel_mechanics_found: L5 endgame is a TORCH-FERRY LOGISTICS puzzle on a closed rectangular rail network (top+bottom horizontal big rails joined by three vertical rails A/B/C spaced exactly one jump-pitch from the socket columns). The single east-network carrier ferries ONE movable torch; parking it on a vertical rail at a peg's row band (or on a horizontal big rail at a peg's column) creates a temporary crossable obstacle exactly between two socket cells, so a lone peg can traverse box-to-box in any direction. The win is a global reduce-to-one plan: 5 pegs (survivor from the west screen + 4 hub pegs) need 4 peg-over-peg removals, and each meeting point must be arranged so the JUMPER survives on a cell from which its next leg is reachable. Also confirmed: the west rail network and east (hub) rail network are permanently disconnected -- the west torch-carrier can never come east, so the endgame must be solved with the east carrier's torch plus the 4 fixed hub torches alone. L6 preview (scouted, not attempted): introduces a color-8 quad block that is ITSELF selectable and movable via the same jump mechanic -- it can jump down over an adjacent peg, and that peg can jump up over it (a second piece type, unknown whether its jumps remove crossed pegs); also a DOUBLE-socket carrier (two 4x4 sockets in one border), and no torches visible in the opening view.
narrative: Resolved the 214-action verified prefix via exp4460's resolver (source: the codex L4 artifact), replayed it against a fresh reset, and confirmed levels_completed=4 at exactly step 214. On L5, instead of merging greedily (the prior session stranded all four hub pegs twice), I first executed the known forced west-screen merge (peg A double-torch-hops east, empty carrier descends the between-boxes rail stub, peg B jumps west over A into the carrier), rode the survivor east across two camera scrolls to the hub, took the one forced removal jump over the first hub peg, and then STOPPED and mapped the entire hub numerically (structure extraction over the raw grid: 4 pegs, 4 fixed torches, one torch-carrying carrier, 3 vertical + 2 horizontal rails). From that world model I derived a complete reduce-to-one line before touching anything: (1) ferry the carrier torch to rail A row-4 and rail B row-4 to walk my survivor into box E next to the E-peg, let the E-peg jump UP over it (removal, jumper survives on top); (2) park the torch on the top big rail to hop the survivor into the NE row as a sacrifice for the NE peg (removal, NE peg lands next to the fixed NE torch); (3) walk the NE peg west over the fixed torch, then down the c16 torch-ladder (top-rail torch park, box-M center torch, bottom-rail torch park, fixed SW torch) into the SE row, and let the SE peg take the final jump west over it. levels_completed hit 5 on that jump at live step 312 with zero resets and zero wasted jumps. Ran the self-verification gate: reproduce() from a fresh reset with the full 312-action sequence returned reached_level=5, reproduced=True. Spent 4 remaining clicks scouting L6 (found the movable color-8 block piece), stopping with budget to spare. gotchas: The game is a free move-enumerator: ACTION6 on any piece paints color-2 markers on every legal landing cell; a silent click (only the row-0 move-counter pixel changes) means zero legal moves. Plan with it constantly -- it never costs more than 1 step.

Carrier rail alignment is exact: a vertical rail's carrier socket straddles the 2px rail line and lands exactly on the crossing cell between two socket columns (e.g. rail A socket = view cols 15-18 bridges box cells at 9-12 and 21-24). Same for horizontal big rails between row bands (r2 rows 12-15 bridges rows 6-9 and 18-21; r6 rows 36-39 bridges 30-33 and 42-45).
Carried torch sprites sit 1px high in their cell (e.g. rows 23-26 against a 24-27 band) -- alignment still counts; trust the move oracle, not pixel equality.

ALL carriers move on every ACTION1-4 press but each is direction-locked to its own rail; carriers at a rail end simply stay. The west-screen carriers drift harmlessly during east-screen carrier routing -- but their drift IS recorded in the action log, so verbatim replay stays deterministic.
The west and east rail networks are DISCONNECTED (gap between world cols ~68-85 on the rows 19-20 rail). Once the survivor rides east, the west torch-carrier is out of the game permanently.

The between-boxes vertical rail stub on the west screen (rows 16-26) is a one-cell staging post: descend one press to the peg row band, and the only forward move is the removal jump east -- the game funnels you.
Jump INTO a carrier requires the carrier socket EMPTY as the landing cell 2 cells beyond a crossed peg/torch; jump OUT works the same way from inside the socket.

Camera scrolls only when the tracked peg moves (rides or jumps) toward the view edge; carrier-only moves never scroll. After any scroll, re-derive the view offset from a known peg before clicking anything (all coordinates are view-relative).

Meeting-point orientation decides who survives a removal: the CROSSED peg dies, the JUMPER survives and must land where its next leg is reachable. Arrange each merge so the survivor is the peg whose onward route exists (e.g. E-peg jumps UP over the sacrifice to land on the box-E top cell, which is one torch-hop from the NE row).

L6: the color-8 quad block is a selectable, movable piece with its own jump moves (it jumped over an adjacent peg in the oracle preview); whether its jump removes the crossed peg is UNTESTED -- test that first next session, it decides whether it is a hazard or a tool.

L6: a double-socket carrier exists (one border, two 4x4 sockets side by side) parked on the east side of the lower box; no torches visible in the L6 opening view, so the 8-block and/or double carrier presumably replace the torch as the traversal mechanism.
